summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would establish an independent guardian to represent unaccompanied non-citizen children seeking protection in Australia and its external territories, including children in detention.
The guardian would arrange care, advocate for children's interests, consult them about decisions and report to Parliament, with their best interests the paramount consideration.
The main provisions would commence within six months of Royal Assent, covering eligible children already in Australia as well as those arriving subsequently.
changes: Removing an unaccompanied child from Australia without the guardian's written consent would become a criminal offence.
The guardian could place children with custodians and change those arrangements.
Covered children could no longer be designated wards of the immigration minister.
The Commonwealth Ombudsman could report on whether a child's detention was appropriate.
summary.affected: Unaccompanied non-citizen children, their custodians, the proposed guardian and the Commonwealth Ombudsman would be affected.
